newsitem.title: CHILE: Banners, tributes as Chile's Pinochet turns 81.
newsitem.headline: Banners, tributes as Chile's Pinochet turns 81.

text.p: Supporters waved banners and chanted the name of General Augusto Pinochet while military chiefs and rightist politicians paid tributes to the former dictator and army head who turned 81 on Monday.

An army band played as Pinochet, who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990, received greetings from armed forces leaders and a small crowd of sympathisers outside his house in Santiago's wealthy eastern suburbs.

"Today the soldiers of Chile's army are paying homage to their commander in chief as he is our leader and in him we see all the qualities of a commander," said Gen. Luis Cortes, head of the Santiago garrison.
Opponents of the military regime, during which more than 3,000 people died in political violence, ignored the celebrations.
Pinochet was appointed as commander in chief of the army in August 1973. Three weeks later he led the bloody military coup which overthrew Marxist President Salvador Allende.

The general commands considerable support among businessmen and right-wing politicians, who credit his government with adopting free-market economic policies which have led to Chile's economic success over the last decade.
This year's celebrations were low-key compared with Pinochet's 80th birthday, which was marked with a parade by thousands of troops and a gala party attended by over 2,000 guests.
